_decision: T115. Which FFmpeg build ships with the application, and where it comes from.
_why_bundled_at_all: FR-112 and R-01: the application downloads nothing on its first run. A person installs
it and prepares a video straight away. Downloading on the person's side would mean a
refusal wherever there is no network, and different versions for different people —
that is, different results from one and the same file.
_why_btbn: The builds are made by an open and reproducible set of scripts, and each has an exact
release tag and a signature over its contents. That is what makes it possible to pin a
particular file rather than "the latest version", which shifts underfoot.
_why_gpl_and_not_lgpl: libx264 is needed — the software encoder the application falls back to when there is no
hardware one (FR-026). It is under GPL-2.0-or-later, and so is an FFmpeg built with it.
Our application is under GPL-3.0-or-later, and the "or later" lets such a build count
An lgpl build would carry no obligations but would come without x264: on a machine with
no suitable graphics card there would be nothing left to prepare a file with.
_why_static: One file instead of a program and a dozen libraries beside it. In an installer that
removes a whole class of trouble: mismatched library versions and "avcodec not found".
_why_branch_8_1_and_not_9_0: 9.0 exists and is newer, but 8.1 is the settled branch one step back. The application's
value is in not spoiling people's videos, and there is no reason to risk that for the
sake of freshness. Moving to 9.0 means re-pinning the fields below (the way
_why_a_month_end_build describes) and running the preparation checks.
_why_a_month_end_build: T719, 2026-10-09. BtbN keeps the last 14 daily builds and the LAST BUILD OF EACH MONTH
for two years (their README, "Release Retention Policy"). The pin before this one was a
daily build, autobuild-2026-08-25-13-06; it was deleted a few weeks later, and with it
both the download in fetch-ffmpeg.mjs and the source link the release depended on.
So the pin is the last build of a month: autobuild-2026-09-30-13-08 stays downloadable
until about September 2028. A newer daily build was there (2026-10-09, n8.1.3-16) but
would vanish again by November and stop the next release in the same place.

_gpl_obligation: We hand out a built FFmpeg, so we are obliged to give its source code too — the very
source this file was built from. Owner's decision 2026-10-09: every release of ours
carries that source itself, as two files beside the installers (release_files below):
FFmpeg at the pinned commit and BtbN's build scripts at the pinned tag's commit. The
scripts pin the exact commit of every library inside the build, x264 included. Links
into somebody else's repository die when the somebody tidies up (that is how the
previous pin was lost); a file attached to our own release lives as long as the release.
Both are packed by scripts/ffmpeg-sources.py from the commits, so the content is what
git verifies against the hash, not whatever an address happened to return.

_release_files: The names do not change from one release to the next, on purpose: the address of the
source of version X is always .../releases/download/vX/ffmpeg-source.tar.gz, so it can
be written down without knowing anything else, and the version inside the archive is
named by its top directory (ffmpeg-<version>/, FFmpeg-Builds-<tag>/).
_verified: The build was made with --enable-gpl --enable-version3, without --enable-nonfree and
without fdk-aac: it may be handed out, and the terms meet our GPL-3.0-or-later
directly rather than through the "or later" clause. Verified by running
The encoders and filters we need are there: libx264 (the software fallback, FR-026),
h264_nvenc (hardware), aac, libvmaf and subtitles. Verified with `ffmpeg -encoders`
and `ffmpeg -filters`, and by the preparation tests run against this very build.
The tag autobuild-2026-09-30-13-08 points at BtbN commit 6c9aec5fc9 (git ls-remote),
and the archive names carry FFmpeg commit 29e619e767 on branch release/8.1.

_size: Each program is about 160 MB (n8.1.3: 157 MB on Windows, 164 MB on Linux): a static
build carries every library inside itself, and in the package they lie there twice
(ffmpeg and ffprobe). A shared build would come out half the weight but
would bring a dozen files beside it and a whole class of "avcodec-NN.dll not found"
